question: Do complementary early measured molecular features support more specific predictions of independently observed clonal fate, with measurement granularity held at single-cell resolution?
status: Frozen before fitting models; feasibility amendments must be recorded separately.
source: CellTag-multi hematopoiesis, DOI 10.1038/s41587-023-01931-4, public processed ML files and clone table
unit: One clone, never one cell or repeated sibling pair. All siblings of an evaluated clone are held out together.
outcome: Published modal day-5 clonal fate. This is a clonal fate prediction, not the exact destiny of the sequenced cell.

cohorts.primary: Clones with early RNA and ATAC measurements and modal fate Mono or Neutro. Chosen before model fitting because these are the two adequately represented committed fates in the common cohort.
cohorts.secondary: All annotated fates in the common paired cohort, using the authors' six fate groups when feasible. Rare classes and missing-training-class failures must be reported, not silently excluded.
cohorts.eligibility: No filtering by prediction quality. Unknown/no-fate clones cannot supply an outcome and are enumerated. Features must come from early day-2.5 cells only.

matching: Use exactly the same clones, outcomes, and partitions for each input condition. Average early measured features within clone and assay for the primary analysis; audit how many cells each mean uses. A one-RNA/one-ATAC-cell sensitivity analysis addresses the effect of averaging.
preprocessing: Inspect supplied matrices for gene/TF features, barcode alignment, normalization and imputation provenance before fitting. Scaling, supervised feature selection, hyperparameter selection, and calibration use training data only. Author-preprocessed representations are explicitly distinguished from a fully prospective end-to-end pipeline.
models: L2 logistic regression and random forest; tune by inner cross-validation log loss with a small fixed grid. Include a training-prior predictor.
validation: Repeated outer clone-disjoint cross-validation. Use paired per-clone Brier/log losses, accuracy, balanced accuracy, AUROC and minority recall. Average repeated losses within clone for paired bootstrap intervals; repetitions are not independent biological samples.
resolution: On separate calibration clones, construct nominal 90% and 80% split-conformal label sets. Evaluate held-out coverage, average set size, singleton fraction, and class-specific coverage. A smaller set supports greater specificity only alongside acceptable held-out coverage. These are operational coverage levels, not biological information ceilings.
negative_control: Break RNA-ATAC clone correspondence without using fate labels, independently within training, calibration and test partitions; refit the same model family. Also assess held-out ATAC permutation for a fixed fitted joint model if useful.

interpretation.positive: Joint early information improves proper held-out scores and can support narrower calibrated outcome sets on the same clones; consistent across simple model families and absent after correspondence is broken.
interpretation.negative: If gains disappear on a common clone-disjoint cohort, the published model comparison does not establish incremental predictive information for this task. Diagnose sampling, evaluation, feature provenance and power before judging the general concept.
interpretation.boundary: No finite model comparison establishes a universal RNA information ceiling. No later state, fate, or fate-informed embedding may enter prediction features. No assertion that a full-gene probability distribution is prohibited.
